subject.title: fix(plugins): deep-clone registry snapshot so nested mutations roll back (#107514)

question: Should plugin-registration transactions guarantee rollback for mutable custom-class instances, or define those instances as immutable opaque values shared by reference?
rationale: Generic reconstruction cannot safely reproduce arbitrary constructors or private fields, while reference sharing intentionally leaves mutations unrolled back; choosing between those guarantees defines the supported plugin-registry contract.

options.title: Adopt immutable opaque instances
options.body: Approve the documented contract that custom-class instances are shared by reference while plain data, collections, and built-in typed values are transactionally restored.

options.title: Require full custom-instance rollback
options.body: Define a supported cloning or registration-value restriction strategy before merge so mutable class-instance state cannot survive rollback.

recommendation.title: Adopt immutable opaque instances
recommendation.body: Approve the documented contract that custom-class instances are shared by reference while plain data, collections, and built-in typed values are transactionally restored.

likelyOwner.reason: The relevant decision belongs to the current-main owner of plugin registration semantics; the available review context does not provide reliable commit attribution.
